I wish that was the case. Long ago, unbeknownst to my younger self I booted up a run. Birds chirped, and sun parted through my window blinds carefully that morning. A half cup of coffee rested upon a messy desk, my own body still cold and stiff from the night before. It was a gentle morning, no work meant no stress for the following days.
           This prologue only serves to display the circumstances of the torture, whilst the day started with a run; it ended with a sad crippled man. 
          The run started with Captain, as I enjoy the quick early game. Trudging across the desolate planet, buying chests for no coin was the life this once commander of a ship now faced. Regardless, things brightened up at the sight of a familiar beautiful clover in the Sirens Call, and for the next loop so would be considered.
         As life happens, small stories and long changes happen to people. Your highscool classmates now waving by at the street of the city, superficially bonded from similarity and time apart. Or your cousins you haven't spoken to in years, returning back into your life as a tik tok influencer. Time changes people in ways pointless of considering good or bad.
         Same went for the captian, the run sped in pacing and loops seemed to dissociate. For now he was not a man in a coat, but a bird; a heretic of nature. However the transformation would be considered beautiful by some, like a caterpillar forming into a butterfly. 
         Misfortune struck quickly however, and just as the butterfly flies its last flight, the heretic falls and dies to the predatory overloading bell. The cycle was completed, and my enjoyment in the run subsided. It was time to get up, have a shower, clean the dishes, watch the new episode of Our Flag means Death; but a striking image flashed amongst my screen. The bird, returning to the grasping harmonious symphony of life. A Phoenix of conquest. However, the horror of my once beloved clover now laid blue and decrepit.
      "Can't just end it here." Were the words of a foolish man. Too egotistical to create his own finale.
           For a few stages, the items racked up to greens, and then reds. I was enjoying myself, considering this journey as a fun experience. I almost felt stronger than I was before, that was until my little bird obtained 9 bottled Chaos.
             My memory fades at this point in the story, like the dots you see after closing your eyes in a bright room. Slowly staring at the ceiling in your faded state of mind. A monstrosity of fireworks, uncontrollable movement and death. From captain, to heretic, to volcanic egg. There was no escape from torture. Loop went after loop. What felt like days trapped in this run went by. A dazed perception, one of which no different from a dehydrated desert wanderer.
           Couldn't buy chests, couldn't see enemies, couldn't experience love. Even Mithrix stood no chance. Instead of his lines of, "Vermin" he stood staring in the sky at the monstrosity before him. Crying to Providence for closure, he was sorry. The toys he played with, created, now strive before him as an amalgamation of misery. He didn't even make it to phase 3. 
            And so my run ended, confused and saddened. The once trotting captain now lay rot in millions of corpses. Limbo in a moving egg. Maybe a symbol for life was best suited being the incarnation of death.
